problem: Visual localization and navigation networks assume static scenes; under object-level dynamics (moved objects) purely visual CNN encoders can match anchor to positive but cannot separate the anchor from nearby negative poses (fine-grained ambiguity).
motivation: Domestic robots doing long-term service face objects moved by humans, so localization must ignore dynamic-object changes while staying sensitive to real pose changes. Static structure (counters, cabinets) is informative while dynamic objects (coffee machine, toaster) are noise, which motivates combining visual and semantic scene-graph reasoning.
key_idea: Fuse a ResNet-50 image embedding with a multi-pathway GCN embedding of an object scene graph (visual, box and GloVe features per object) and train with a cascaded triplet contrastive loss to get a scene embedding whose cosine similarity is robust to object dynamics.
insight: Cascaded triplets with graded position deviations and 50% same-pose different-layout positives teach the network which changes are allowed. CNN baselines learn A-P matching but fail on A-N ambiguity; adding scene-graph semantics fixes this, shown by triplet tests over 20 rooms and lower localization failure in the navigation test (13.2% vs 25.5-95.2% for baselines on the same navigator). No component ablation is reported.
method: Image branch: ResNet-50 split into C4 backbone and 5th-stage head, giving a 2048-d image embedding from a 224x224 RGB image and RoI-aligned per-object visual features.

Object feature embedding: concatenates a 256-d sinusoidal bounding-box embedding x_b, a 2048-d RoI visual feature x_v and a 300-d GloVe word embedding x_w, passed through an fcn to give the node feature x_i.

Multi-pathway GCN: the adjacency matrix is split by edge type (on, in, proximity; disjoint dropped), each processed by its own 3-layer GCN pathway. The three outputs are concatenated (6144-d) and mapped by an fcn to a 2048-d scene-graph embedding.

Scene embedding and similarity: image and graph embeddings are fused into a 2048-d vector; a Siamese setup uses cosine similarity, with threshold eps=0.90 chosen statistically for same-pose localization.

Cascaded contrastive learning: triplet loss with margin 0.1 on a triplet dataset with graded Manhattan deviations (50/20/15/10/5% mix), where 50% of anchor-positive pairs are same pose with different object layouts.
Scene graph extraction: heuristic from AI2THOR ground truth (on from simulator; in and proximity from 3D bounding boxes).

Navigation application: topological map with 4 heading sub-nodes per node, Dijkstra planning, VGG16 visual navigator (SPTM-style) for translation actions, and the similarity localizer decides segment completion.

setting.backbone: ResNet-50 + GCN (ImageNet-pretrained init, trained with triplet loss); VGG16 visual navigator
setting.training_data: 9.5k triplets from AI2THOR (21 train / 4 val / 5 test rooms per each of 4 room types, 30 instances each) with object dynamics; ImageNet-pretrained init
setting.observation: monocular RGB image plus scene graph (object labels and 2D boxes; GT-derived in simulation)
setting.action_space: discrete grid moves: forward/left/right translation of 0.25 m and rotate left/right 90°
setting.privileged: scene graph and object labels/boxes derived from simulator ground truth; real-world examples had manually labeled boxes and graphs; topological map built beforehand

numbers.extra: 20 test rooms, 5476 neighbour cases, max 12 steps; GT-derived scene graphs

numbers_note: Abstract reports 85.02% triplet similarity accuracy but the per-model results are only in a figure and the body gives no exact value. Navigation table has neighbour (N) and arbitrary (A) columns; total cases 5476 / 204136.
results: SeanNet beats ResNet50, ResNext50, VGG16 and GoogleNet on triplet similarity across 20 unseen test rooms (85.02% per the abstract). In navigation with the same navigator it gets 80.2%/65.2% SR (neighbour/arbitrary), versus the strongest baseline GoogleNet at 69.4%/30.6%.
limitations: Scene graphs come from simulator ground truth or manual labeling; no learned scene-graph generator is evaluated.
Evaluated mainly in AI2THOR on a discrete grid with four headings; real-world evidence is a few qualitative examples; no ablations and lighting changes are out of scope.
Small triplet dataset (9.5k) and hand-tuned similarity threshold.
